newsitem.title: USA: Coleman names Jerry Levin chairman.
newsitem.headline: Coleman names Jerry Levin chairman.

text.p: Coleman Co Inc said Tuesday it named Jerry Levin chairman and acting chief executive officer.
Levin replaces Michael Hammes, who is leaving the cmopany, it said.
Coleman, which makes camping gear and other products, also said it expects to report a net loss for the fourth quarter of 1996 of about $37 million.

Coleman said the loss was due primarily to a number of one-time factors including the costs of integrating the Camping Gaz business into the company and coil light patent litigation settlement and costs related to the discontinuation of certain products.
It said operating income for all of 1996 is expected to be about $70 million, with net income at about $10 million or $0.19 a share, before restructuring and other charges.
It said restructuring and other charges previously announced in the third quarter and additional charges in connection with the coil light settlement total about $55 million after taxes.
This will result in a 1996 net loss of about $45 million or $0.85 a share, it said. Coleman reported a net income of $39 million or $0.74 a share for 1995.
Levin is a past chairman and has been a director of Coleman since 1989.
Levin is also executive vice president of MacAndrews & Forbes Holdings Inc, which owns about 83 percent of Coleman's outstanding common stock, and chairmam of Revlon Inc.
Coleman said it has initiated a search for a chief executive and Levin will remain as chairman following completion of the search.
